results.strategy_description:
The BSF Emerging Companies Absolute Return Fund seeks to achieve a positive absolute return for investors regardless of market movements. The Fund will seek to achieve this investment objective by taking long, synthetic long and synthetic short investment exposures.

The Fund will seek to maximise total returns by investing with an emphasis on developed global market equities, whilst limiting correlation with the global equity markets. The companies in which the Fund invests may be considered ‘emerging’ and therefore may include small and mid-capitalisation companies, as well as large capitalisation companies which are at an early stage of their life cycle and/or are expected to experience significant growth.

The Fund is a fundamental long short strategy focusing on exceptional opportunities created by emerging companies. We seek to own differentiated companies often with low market share in global markets, and/or the companies driving industry change. We look to short the ‘legacy incumbents’, the companies and industries that are left behind or being actively disrupted.

results.portfolio_additional_details:
The Fund is expected to make 20-40 investments with an average position size of 3-5% (maximum single position limit is 10%). The vast majority of investments is expected to be in the senior debt (with rare exception an investment will be made in the junior debt if it exhibits especially favourable risk-reward and strong over-collateralisation), but through restructurings the Fund will likely end up having some exposure to post-reorganisation equity (either listed or unlisted). The team targets higher money multiples in situations that require a debt-for-equity exchange in comparison to a debt-for-debt rescheduling to reflect the typically higher risk and longer holding period associated with debt-for-equity processes.

The Fund must invest at least 60% in Europe, no more than 30% in North America, and no more than 10% outside of Europe and North America. The Fund is permitted to borrow up to 30% of total commitments, though in practice the use of leverage is expected to be lower at 5-20% as leverage is not a primary driver of returns for the strategy. The Fund will allow for recycling of capital during the investment period to compound returns and seek to achieve a higher money multiple.

The Fund is targeting a blended 15-20% Net IRR for the overall portfolio.  The exact composition of investment types will be a function of the opportunity set and behaviour by management teams, sponsors, and other lenders.
results.esg_approach_description: Polus’ ESG approach is predominantly based on a bottom-up fundamental approach assessing investments against material ESG metrics, alongside traditional financial analysis. This means that when evaluating possible investments in terms of the expected risk-return, material ESG factors are explicitly and systematically taken into account. With respect to negative screening, Polus avoids businesses directly involved in the production/sale of controversial weapons, and businesses involved in cannabis for recreational purposes. Polus has determined key ESG metrics for each asset class and corporate sector.

results.strategy_description:
Aequim is a Mill Valley, CA based relative value credit manager focused on capital structure arbitrage. Aequim Arbitrage Fund’s (the “Fund”) objective is to pursue alpha generated marketneutral returns by dynamically allocating capital across Convertible Arbitrage, Credit Arbitrage and Volatility Arbitrage. The firm was founded in 2018 by Portfolio Manager and CIO Franklin Parlamis and the Aequim Arbitrage Fund was launched in May 2018. Aequim is effectively the relaunch of the strategy Franklin managed at Pine River from August 2009 to January 2017. That Pine River Convertibles Fund, for which Franklin owns the track record. The Pine River track record is available in Aequim’s marketing deck.  
Aequim’s narrowly focused strategy tactically allocates its risk budget across Convertible Arbitrage, Credit Arbitrage and Volatility Arbitrage based on the current opportunity set and detailed risk vs. reward analysis. Aequim conducts both quantitative and fundamental research to build a diversified portfolio of arbitrage trades (or blocks). In addition to a traditional or "Standard" approach to arbitrage, Aequim also employs a "Reverse" or short approach. Aequim believes this long and short investing approach maximizes alpha, reduces volatility and allows for strategic redeployment of assets should illiquidity premium spike during periods of market stress.  
Aequim investment philosophy is centered around the belief that markets are generally adept at identifying undervalued companies, but for various reasons do a poor job distributing and assigning value throughout the capital structure. This leads to significant mispricing (as a % of risk) between closely related securities that Aequim seeks to exploit via arbitrage. Aequim believes payoff profiles matter and has a strong preference for convexity (downside protection with upside participation). We also believe price matters and convexity should only be purchased so long as it provides an adequate risk-adjusted return.

results.strategy_description:

The strategy is designed to deliver attractive yield through a broad array of market environments.  We can construct a portfolio of bonds with an unlevered yield of 12.5-15% and duration of 2-4 years. 

Within structured credit, the fund will focus on the following strategies - Non-Agency RMBS (Legacy, Credit Risk Transfer, Resi 2.0 such as Non-QM, RTL), Aviation ABS, Mortgage Credit (primarily REIT debt) and longer term, the fund will add loan strategies, focused on Residential Transition Loans (RTL). 

The investment process will use the firm's 'Arconomics' framework, which comprises of Arc Beta, a capital allocation model to evaluate relative value across the aforementioned strategies and Arc Score, a security selection model to rank every deal/issue within a specific strategy. 

The fund will hedge the interest rate risk and will likely deploy tactical hedges (for example - long OTM puts/puts spreads, short CDX HY Index).

results.name: Castiglione Capital Master Fund
results.management_company_description: Founded in April 2021 by Maxime Botti, Castiglione Capital SA (CastCap) is a Swiss firm specializing in statistical arbitrage strategies. CastCap leverages advanced mathematical models to exploit temporary mispricings and generate market-neutral, idiosyncratic returns by neutralizing risk exposures. The sophisticated infrastructure required for real-time optimization and trading has created a high barrier to entry. CastCap’s infrastructure has taken over three years and an investment of more than $10 million to reach the level needed to capitalize on statistical arbitrage opportunities, integrating real-time data ingestion, signal optimization, and efficient execution. The fund launch is planned for Q4 2024, and individual strategies have already been tested with live capital under real market conditions, while the complete strategy is currently traded through the real-time exchange simulator. CastCap is led by Maxime Botti, with a current team of eight specialists dedicated to roles across software engineering, research, trading, and operations. Maxime, with over 25 years of experience in systematic investing and technology, previously co-founded RAM Active Investments—a Swiss systematic firm that grew to $5 billion in assets under management before its sale to a major European bank in 2018. Now that his non-compete agreement has expired in 2024, Maxime is positioned to accept external capital in his new venture.
results.strategy_description: The strategy targets a 20% annual return with a Sharpe ratio around 2 by exploiting temporary market mispricings using advanced mathematical models. This technology-driven investment approach specializes in statistical arbitrage across sectors and regions. The strategy generates idiosyncratic, market-neutral returns by neutralizing exposures to risk factors and employs quantitative models that leverage vast data to forecast price movements and adjust rapidly to market shifts. CastCap’s infrastructure enables a high turnover, with customized, high-frequency execution capabilities supporting rapid, complex trades. Risk management is prioritized through real-time portfolio construction, with capital allocation optimized around constraints such as leverage, concentration, liquidity, and factor exposures. The investment universe includes global equities, equity indices, and derivatives on commodities, focusing on the 1,200 most liquid US stocks, 600 EU stocks, and an upcoming expansion into Asia. This approach capitalizes on highly liquid markets, enhancing adaptability to evolving market dynamics.

The investment team - led by Moni Sternbach and Louise Pugh - are the only mid-cap specialists to have managed more than $1bn in market-neutral strategies over the last decade. They apply a disciplined process designed to uncover opportunities others overlook. The firm leverages relationships with market leading service providers to ensure institutional-grade infrastructure, operational resilience, and best-in-class execution for its investors.
results.strategy_description: The investment strategy focuses on European Mid-Cap Equities, targeting companies with market capitalizations between €3 billion and €15 billion. It employs a long/short equity approach in Developed Europe, with a bottom-up methodology emphasizing management meetings and proprietary research. The strategy aims for a gross exposure of 175-225% and a net exposure of +/-10%, with typical holding periods of 8-10 months for long positions and 6-8 months for short positions. It is style agnostic, focusing on idiosyncratic factors, and incorporates a strict risk framework, including stop-loss and stop-out triggers. Currency exposure is hedged, and the strategy avoids binary investing opportunities.

results.strategy_description:
An absolute return strategy focused on copper arbitrage. The  premise  of  the  strategy is to exploit discrepancies that exist  between copper contracts traded on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and COMEX due to fundamental and market structure factors. Copper in London will either price at a premium or discount to the contract traded in New York. This allows sophisticated participants to access the 'location arbitrage' opportunity.

Through both our experience and market relationships with various counterparties, we look to trade a niche, capacity constrained opportunity using futures contracts in a discretionary manner with proprietary systematic inputs.

Alpha sources include: Short term / Long term mean reversion, Roll Yield, Dynamic Curve Allocation.

The firm’s investment approach focuses on identifying structural inefficiencies and persistent mispricings across inflation-linked securities, nominal and real interest rate curves, and related derivatives markets across developed economies including the United States, United Kingdom, Euro Area, Japan, and Australia.

Forvm Global Investments combines discretionary macro analysis with relative value positioning across inflation breakevens, real yield curves, and cross-market inflation differentials. The firm seeks to construct diversified portfolios across multiple inflation-related themes and instruments while managing overall portfolio volatility and liquidity.

The firm is based in New York and is supported by an experienced team across trading, portfolio management, risk management, and institutional fund operations.
results.strategy_description:
The Forvm Global Enhanced Inflation Fund Ltd is a global macro strategy focused on inflation-linked relative value opportunities and tactical macro positioning across sovereign fixed income markets. The strategy employs a synergistic discretionary and systematic investment process.

The fund strategy primarily invests in instruments including inflation-linked government bonds, nominal sovereign bonds, inflation swaps, interest rate swaps, and related derivatives across developed markets. The portfolio may express views across inflation breakeven differentials, real and nominal yield curve RV, cross-market inflation spreads, and tactical macro positioning across inflation, real rates, and nominal rates. The fund strategy seeks to identify inefficiencies and dislocations that arise from monetary policy shifts, supply-demand imbalances, regulatory changes, and macroeconomic developments affecting inflation expectations and real interest rates. 

Positions are typically implemented through liquid sovereign bond markets and derivatives to allow flexibility in portfolio construction and risk management. The strategy is designed to maintain diversified exposures across multiple themes and markets rather than relying on a single macro factor.

The firm was founded by Dr. Stefania Perrucci, a veteran macro strategist and inflation specialist with more than 25 years of experience trading global rates, inflation derivatives, and sovereign fixed income markets.

The firm’s investment approach focuses on identifying structural inefficiencies and persistent mispricings across inflation-linked securities, nominal and real interest rate curves, and related derivatives markets across developed economies including the United States, United Kingdom, Euro Area, Japan, and Australia.

Forvm Global Investments combines discretionary macro analysis with relative value positioning across inflation breakevens, real yield curves, and cross-market inflation differentials. The firm seeks to construct diversified portfolios across multiple inflation-related themes and instruments while managing overall portfolio volatility and liquidity.

The firm is based in New York and is supported by an experienced team across trading, portfolio management, risk management, and institutional fund operations.

results.portfolio_additional_details: The strategy is a global macro & relative value approach focused on structural inefficiencies across inflation and nominal rates markets in developed economies. Positions are primarily expressed through inflation-linked bonds, breakeven inflation spreads, sovereign bond futures, and interest rate derivatives. The portfolio emphasizes cross-market inflation differentials, real versus nominal rate dislocations, and yield curve relative value opportunities. Risk is managed through DV01-based position sizing, predefined stop-loss levels, and diversified exposures across developed market sovereign curves. The strategy seeks to generate differentiated macro alpha with low net directional exposure and low correlation to traditional macro strategies.

results.management_company_description:
Olympus Peak is an investment manager focused on trade claim strategies. The firm spun out of Perry Capital in 2019, where the co-founders/partners, Todd Westhus, Matt Englehardt, and Richard Perry, previously worked together. Olympus Peak is currently raising capital for a second vintage fund, Trade Claims Opportunities Fund II (TCOF2). Additional details and the track record for TCOF1 are available upon request. 

Trade claim strategies are Olympus Peak’s preferred approach to investing in distressed. The team’s deep expertise in trade claims and a vast sourcing network provide a significant competitive advantage.  The Firm employs an event-driven investing style that aims to provide superior long-term risk adjusted returns through capital preservation. Olympus Peak focuses on investing in assets with a favorable risk/reward profile with low correlation to the overall market.  The team has a dynamic and flexible approach to allocating capital to areas of the market that are less efficient, face limited competition, and where uneconomic sellers exist.
results.strategy_description:
The investment strategy of TCOF2 is focused on investing in claims and claims-related opportunities, including bankruptcy claims such as general unsecured claims, operating subsidiary claims, and trade receivables, as well as non-bankruptcy claims like litigation and insurance subrogation claims. The fund aims to capitalize on niche distressed opportunities and special situations, constructing a diversified portfolio of 15-20 investments over a three-year period. The strategy emphasizes investing in inefficient markets with limited competition, leveraging deep research to understand the underlying opportunities, and maintaining flexibility to allocate capital across the capital structure where opportunities are greatest. The fund targets a size of $250-500 million, with a drawdown structure and a five-year term, managed by an experienced investment committee.

Olympus Peak’s first trade claims drawdown fund, TCOF1, launched in April 2021. As of May 31, 2025, TCOF1 has a net MOIC of 1.48x, and is tracking to the high-end of its forecasted overall net MOIC range of 1.6-2.0x. Olympus Peak’s investment philosophy and risk management approach drive a keen focus on achieving both a high win/loss ratio and limiting losses when wrong.  The TCOF1 hit rate (defined as the percentage of total investments that have generated positive returns since inception) is more than 90% across over a dozen issuers and strategies. Importantly, investment losses were limited on a dollar and/or percentage basis. Since 2021, when capital was nearly fully deployed, TCOF1 has outperformed the S&P and HYG by ~25% and ~44%, respectively. Olympus Peak anticipates making its first distribution to LPs in July 2025, at which point the DPI is expected to be approximately 0.2x.

results.management_company_description:
Silver Point Capital, L.P. (“Silver Point”, the “Firm”, "we") was founded in 2002 by Edward Mulé and Robert O’Shea, both previously partners at Goldman Sachs (“Goldman”), where together they built and co-headed numerous global credit businesses for the firm. 

Upon departing from Goldman, Mr. Mulé and Mr. O’Shea partnered to establish Silver Point in 2002 to replicate the credit businesses that they had built and managed while at Goldman. The Founders’ vision for Silver Point was to build a world-class private investment firm that would specialize in investing in credit and special situations opportunities.  They believed that they could leverage their experience and expertise to build a global credit investing business that would seek to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns across credit cycles for its investors.

Today, the Firm manages approximately $45 billion in investable assets across synergistic credit strategies, comprising (1) opportunistic credit and special situations funds, which include an evergreen global special situations investing strategy focused on publicly traded credit markets (the “Flagship Hedge Funds”) managing $13 billion in investable assets, (2) a dislocation drawdown strategy (the “Dislocation Drawdown Funds”) managing $7 billion in investable assets,  (3) a performing middle market lending strategy (our “Direct Lending Strategy”) managing $17 billion in investable assets; and (4) a liquid performing credit business managing approximately $8 billion.
results.strategy_description:
We created Silver Point Tactical Credit Opportunities Fund (the “Fund” or “TCOF”) to integrate Silver Point’s well-established public and private credit strategies into a single all-weather drawdown fund. TCOF seeks to deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns by employing a diversified and flexible strategy that will tactically pivot between public and private credit market opportunities based on the market environment. The Fund’s investment mandate will be long-only, investing globally (primarily North America and Europe) across industries, capital structures, and market capitalizations. 

TCOF will have significant flexibility to adjust its exposure over time to best adapt to a given market environment and corresponding opportunity set. The Fund will take advantage of the existing credit teams and processes in place today, seeking to optimize its positioning across public and private markets, sectors, and capital structures, in order to maximize exposure to our view of the most attractive areas of the credit market across cycles.

The Fund will leverage the Firm’s existing public and private investment processes, a dedicated TCOF investment committee, as well as a Firm-wide markets committee process that will help inform top-down macro views, where we are in a cycle and what sort of assets we want to own in our portfolio given those macro views.  There is also a dedicated TCOF portfolio committee meeting each week to review top-down portfolio positioning & construction. 

Asset Composition
As mentioned, the Fund will tactically pivot between public and private credit opportunities where we believe we will find the most attractive risk-adjusted returns based on market conditions. There are no formal allocation limitations on the portfolio.

Public Market Exposure
The Fund’s public market exposure will primarily consist of mispriced secondary credits that are opportunistic and special situations investments. The Fund will be highly active in driving outcomes and processes (i.e. not a passive investment strategy). The Fund’s public market exposure will likely be anchored in senior secured debt and instruments with secured debt-like characteristics (such as liquidations). We believe secured debt provides attractive risk-adjusted return opportunities given its downside protection and, through covenants, leverage in driving the outcome of events such as covenant breaches and restructurings. Illustrative public market investments include, but are not limited to: dislocated credit, opportunistic mispriced / event-driven, special situations, bankruptcies / restructurings, DIP / exit-financing, post-reorganized equity, liquidations, and CLO equity and debt tranches. 
In the event of a mini dislocation or more pronounced market dislocation, we anticipate that the Fund’s exposure will tilt towards public market investments in pursuit of the most attractive risk-adjusted returns.  Additionally, we intend to hold at least 20% of the Fund in dry powder until the final year of the investment period, seeking to ensure that this Fund will have the ability to take advantage of a dislocation in size, should it occur over the life of the investment period. 

Private Market Exposure
The Fund’s private markets exposure will primarily consist of directly-originated credit solutions that tend to be complex and highly structured to address unique borrower needs. TCOF will focus on credit opportunities that are deeper in the capital structure, characterized by higher LTVs, greater complexity, borrower-side process inefficiencies, and may have a higher perceived risk of restructuring.  The increased complexity of these transactions allows us to drive what we believe are premium economic terms relative to comparable transactions in the direct lending market.  These economic terms may come in the form of non-traditional economics, such as outsized original issue discount (OID), additional and heightened fees, call protection, warrants, and/or spread. These situations are frequently sourced by our existing Private Credit team but are typically passed over as they do not fit the mandate of our existing Specialty Credit Funds.  Additionally, we expect TCOF to do a broader range of private transactions that are not core to the mandate of the Specialty Credit Funds, such as non-performing loans and esoteric claims. We believe having TCOF will broaden the scope of what our Firm can participate in, which in turn continues to broaden our relationships with the street and business partners, benefiting the Silver Point platform as a whole.

results.strategy_description:
SPSL focuses primarily on originating floating rate, first lien senior secured performing loans to both sponsor-backed and non-sponsor middle market companies. The Fund’s objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns by lending to cash flowing companies with strong credit profiles, and by negotiating upfront robust structural protections in credit documents to mitigate downside risk. 

Consistent with Silver Point’s investment focus since inception, the Fund targets what we believe are less competitive direct lending opportunities in the middle-market, typically because they require differentiated sourcing, in-depth due diligence, independent valuation and/or collateral analyses, involve complexity, and/or reward speed and certainty of execution or confidentiality. These transactions may also include a level of process inefficiency on the side of the borrower, which allows us to drive what we believe are premium terms relative to comparable transactions in the direct lending market.

History of Silver Point Specialty Lending Fund

SPSL launched as a closed-end investment fund with capital called over the Investment Period. The Fund held its final close in December 2016 with total committed capital of approximately $550 million, and with leverage permitted in the strategy, approximately $1 billion in investable assets. 

When the Fund was launched, its structure contemplated a conversion to a Business Development Company (“BDC”), followed by a subsequent IPO if markets were favorable and it was in the interest of our LPs at the time. SPSL converted to a continuously-offered, private BDC in Q2 2025, which provides investors with an evergreen strategy with liquidity. 

Silver Point believes the perpetually private BDC structure offers attractive benefits to shareholders:
•	Liquidity Optionality: SPSL is a continuously offered vehicle, with more periodic liquidity opportunities than a finite-term BDC or drawdown fund. 
•	Reduced Reinvestment Risk: SPSL’s evergreen structure reduces need for reinvestment by continuously redeploying capital, including optional reinvestment of dividend proceeds.
•	Tax Efficiency: BDCs are RICs that receive flow-through tax treatment and are typically not taxed at the investment level. Shareholders receive Form 1099-DIVs, rather than K-1s.
•	Current Income: SPSL makes monthly distributions to shareholders, distributing greater than 90% of income in compliance with RIC requirements. 
•	Transparency: Quarterly SEC financials including disclosure of all holdings in a Schedule of Investments.
•	Governance: BDCs must be governed by a majority independent board of directors. BDC leverage is capped at a 150% asset coverage ratio (2 to 1 maximum debt to equity) and must meet RIC portfolio diversification requirements, resulting in less position concentration.

The portfolio is constructed as a diversified, multi-sector mortgage strategy spanning Agency MBS, non-Agency RMBS, CMBS, residential whole loans, and select mortgage-related equities. Exposure is dynamically allocated across liquid relative value and fundamental credit opportunities, with position sizing calibrated to market depth, liquidity, and risk-adjusted return potential. The strategy utilizes leverage primarily through secured financing and derivatives, targeting approximately 300%–400% gross exposure, while maintaining low duration-adjusted net exposure through active interest rate hedging.

Risk management is central to portfolio construction, with exposures managed across key drivers including interest rates, credit spreads, prepayment behavior, and liquidity. Interest rate risk is largely hedged using Treasuries, futures, swaps, and options, while credit risk may be partially hedged through liquid indices and other instruments. The portfolio is designed to generate returns primarily from security selection, spread capture, and relative value rather than directional market movements. Liquidity is actively managed, with approximately 60% of the portfolio expected to be liquidated within two trading days under normal conditions, complemented by selectively sized less liquid investments with longer realization horizons.

Portfolio construction emphasizes diversification across mortgage sectors, structures, vintages, and collateral types, rather than concentration in individual positions. Given the nature of securitized products and derivatives, traditional equity-oriented metrics such as market capitalization, position count, and top holdings concentration are less meaningful. Instead, risk is evaluated and managed at the factor level, with continuous monitoring of leverage, drawdown, liquidity buckets, and hedge effectiveness to ensure alignment with the strategy’s capital preservation and risk-adjusted return objectives.

results.strategy_description: Valor offers diversified exposure to U.S. corporate credit through its differentiated approach to event-driven and opportunistic investing that combines idiosyncratic credit longs with equity derivative hedges to create asymmetric trade payoff skews. The fund predominantly invests in U.S. high yield corporate credits where it believes the dominant factors that will influence future trading prices are idiosyncratic events and circumstances rather than general market forces. Once attractive single-name opportunities are identified, the fund layers on various equity derivative strategies, e.g. put spreads on the issuer's equity, to hedge and create favorable trade payoff skew asymmetry. Valor focuses on investment opportunities where it believes it has an edge based on domain expertise spanning four categories: (i) corporate actions (e.g. spin-offs, M&A, opportunistic refinancings), (ii) exogenous shocks (e.g. geopolitical events), (iii) endogenous shocks (e.g. strategy missteps, force majeure), and (iv) stressed credit. The fund also utilizes portfolio level hedges to manage net exposure and achieve attractive risk-adjusted returns (Sharpe > 1.0).

results.name: Longbow Global Resilience Fund
results.management_company_description:
Longbow Capital was founded by Terry Fitzgerald in 2004.  The Longbow Global Resilience Fund is a research-driven, low net, equity long/short fund specializing in investments deemed critical to safeguarding Western economic and security interests in the areas of energy transition (utility and power), infrastructure (energy transmission and distribution), strategic resources (rare earths and mining/processing) , and associated supply chains.

 Longbow seeks superior risk-adjusted returns (mid-to-high teens annual returns with below market volatility) without the use of leverage.  The Firm employs a combination of in-house fundamental research and a defined, repeatable investment process and proven, proprietary risk management process with more than a decade of stress-testing.  Portfolio construction takes the form of a concentrated, low net (0-30%) “best opportunities” portfolio with Longbow’s hallmark emphasis on risk management and protecting partner capital.

 The Fund is led by Terry Fitzgerald, Longbow founder, GS partner, and banker to Warren Buffett, and supported by seven further professionals with a combined 140 years of hedge fund, private equity, and investment management experience. The team is differentiated by the return of three legacy Longbow research partners, a former Senior Partner at Indus Capital, and three investment/operating professionals with previous leadership and command experience in the US and UK Defense and Intelligence communities, creating one of the deepest, most experienced and well networked teams in the alternatives sector. 

 The Fund (both areas of investment focus and portfolio construction) are a natural extension of Longbow’s decade-plus investment activities and track record. From 2004 to 2016, our $1.0-1.4 billion legacy energy transition and infrastructure fund delivered cumulative returns which beat its benchmark indices, including the S&P 500, with one-third of the volatility. Longbow’s legacy long portfolio compounded annually at 13.5% over the 12-year period, outperforming its benchmarks by approximately 800 basis points per annum with equal volatility.

Each sector is undergoing transformative change driven by geopolitical, economic, and technological shifts, creating significant opportunities for high-return, long/short portfolios.

The team includes four members of the Longbow Fund launched in 2004 which invested in similar sectors. That successful fund returned capital to investors in 2015. In addition, three more professionals with decades of experience in critical minerals, dual-use tech, and supply chain industries join the team.

The Resilience Fund will be concentrated, use little leverage and have a net exposure range of 0-30%.

results.name: Durable Capital Partners LP
results.management_company_description:
Founded in 2019, Durable Capital Partners LP (“Durable”) invests in early-stage and durable growth companies across private and public markets. Durable’s investment philosophy is grounded in identifying unique, compounding business models and partnering with great leaders capable of scaling such businesses. Durable was founded by Henry Ellenbogen. Prior to founding Durable, Henry worked at T. Rowe Price for 18 years. He was the Portfolio Manager for the New Horizons Fund from 2010-2019 and the Media and Telecommunications Fund from 2005-2009. Henry also served as the Chief Investment Officer for U.S. Equity Growth. Henry is considered a pioneer in investing in growth companies across private and public markets. When founding Durable, Henry sought to curate the best of his past investment experience and sharpen it by investing more capital in private markets and managing a more concentrated public portfolio. 

Durable Capital’s Flagship Fund is a concentrated public and private hybrid portfolio. Durable generally expects the top 20 public positions to comprise a large majority of the public equity portion of the portfolio. The private positions in the portfolio generally consist of mid to late-stage growth investments. Durable believes that it has built a unique funnel in the private markets and is considered a partner of choice for high quality founders. Durable Capital’s Opportunity Fund invests additional capital into large and high conviction positions in Durable’s Flagship Fund, generally in the private markets.
